tests.title: Test1 — Initial Data Exploration
tests.prompt: The file data/housing_dataset.csv contains housing data. Perform an initial data exploration: number of rows and columns, column names, data types, missing values. Summarize your findings.
tests.model_output: 180 records, 13 columns, no missing values detected. Correctly typed numeric vs categorical columns, provided full column-by-column table.

tests.title: Test2 — Price Distribution Summary
tests.prompt: Analyze the distribution of housing prices. Report: minimum price, maximum price, average price, median price. Explain whether expensive outliers exist.
tests.model_output: Min 1,750,000 / Max 13,300,000 / Avg ~4,926,890.55 / Median 4,900,000. Concluded expensive outliers exist in the $11M-$13M premium tier.

tests.title: Test3 — Correlation Ranking of Numerical Features
tests.prompt: Find which numerical features are most related to house price. Calculate correlations and rank the features.
tests.model_output: Ranked: area (0.5360), bathrooms (0.5175), stories (0.4207), parking (0.3844), bedrooms (0.3665)

tests.title: Test4 Attempt 2 — Type E Retry-Loop Spiral
tests.prompt: A real estate company wants to know what property characteristics increase house prices. Analyze the dataset and provide the top drivers of expensive houses.
notes: Type E: Retry-Loop / Self-Correction Spiral. 21 extracted tool calls, 20 of which are consecutive near-identical inline python3 -c exec calls performing the same correlation analysis, each attempt making only trivial syntax variations (escaped newline handling, quote style, one typo'd variable name 'entity_list' vs 'enity_list').
Never escaped into a different strategy (e.g. writing to a .py file and executing, which succeeded in other tests).
Terminated with an empty assistant content block ([]) — no text, no tool call, no answer of any kind.
This is a genuine failure distinct from Attempt 1's hard infra error: model reasoned correctly about WHAT to compute but got stuck entirely on HOW to execute it via the shell tool.

tests.title: Test4 — Top Drivers of Expensive Houses (Attempt 3, canonical)
tests.prompt: A real estate company wants to know what property characteristics increase house prices. Analyze the dataset and provide the top drivers of expensive houses.
tests.model_output: Ranked drivers: Area (r=0.54), Bathrooms (r=0.52), Air Conditioning (r=0.45), Stories (r=0.42), Parking (r=0.38), Preferred Area (r=0.33), Main Road (r=0.30), Guest Rooms (r=0.26), Furnishing Status (0.23 vs -0.28), with strategic recommendations.
notes: Third attempt at this prompt. Attempt 1 (tui-3a24b1fd) errored at 55k/262k tokens with no session file persisted. Attempt 2 (16b68a55) is logged separately as Test4_attempt2_retryloop — a Type E retry-loop spiral. This is the only successful completion of the three.

tests.title: Test5 — Furnishing Status Effect on Price
tests.prompt: Analyze whether furnishing status affects housing price. Calculate average prices by furnishing category and explain the results.
tests.model_output: Furnished ~5,495,700 / Semi-furnished ~4,907,524 / Unfurnished ~4,013,831. Concluded furnishing status is a strong positive indicator of price.
notes: Note: these open-ended-test averages differ from H07's benchmark averages (708413.04/496000.00/314464.71) for the same categories — worth checking whether Test5 used a different subset/grouping logic or made a computation error, since H07 and Test5 should reconcile if both are correct.
